layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: INTRODUCTION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ThE coRrosion resistance of stainless steels is intimately related to their passivation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: behaviour. Generally, the higher the chromium content the more passivation is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: facilitated and chemical stability improved.1,2 Other elements are usually added to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: modify the structure and mechanical properties of the alloys and/or to increase

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion resistance.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The most common alloying element is nickel which is an austenite former.³ In

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: certain environments the presence of nickel may have a beneficial effect on corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: behaviour. For example, in sulfuric acid solution it decreases the passivation current

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: density and the current density in the passive state.4 On the other hand, nickel has

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hardly any influence on the value of the pitting potential in chloride media.2,7 The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: beneficial effect of molybdenum in increasing the resistance of stainless steels to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting corrosion has been known for many years8,9 but is not yet sufficiently

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: understood.10,11 Tungsten has been reported to improve resistance to pitting corro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sion of both ferritic and austenitic alloys.8,9,12,13 In austenitic stainless steels silicon as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: well as vanadium have been found to increase the value of the pitting potential.12 On

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the other hand, manganese, due to sulfide formation, promotes pitting.14 Other

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: metallic elements studied include copper5,15,16 and rhenium.12,17 Carbide forming

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: elements such as titanium, niobium and tantalum are frequently added in small

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: concentrations to austenitic stainless steels to reduce their susceptibility to inter-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: granular corrosion.5,18 According to Tomashov et al.12 titanium increases and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: niobium and tantalum decrease the value of the pitting potential.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In our laboratory the reaction mechanism by which molybdenum improves the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion resistance of iron-chromium alloys in chloride media is being studied by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: electrochemical and surface analytical techniques.10,11,13,19,20 In this context it was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: considered of interest to compare the effect of alloyed molybdenum with that of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: other metals such as tungsten, vanadium and silicon that might exhibit similar

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: behaviour. For that purpose, these elements were alloyed to binary Fe-Cr alloys in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: equal and relatively high atomic concentration. A comparison of the effect of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: different alloying elements must be done based on equal value of atomic rather than

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: weight percent because large density differences between different alloying elements

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: may otherwise lead to wrong conclusions. The use of a relatively high concentration

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is indicated to improve the signal to noise ratio of surface analytical measurements.

layout_dets.text: EXPERIMENTAL METHOD

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The chemical composition of the alloys used is given in Table 1. The binary Fe-Cr alloys were furnished

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by Climax Molybdenum. They were subsequently hot forged. The other alloys were prepared in our

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: laboratory by alloying to the original Fe-Cr alloys the elements Mo, W, V or Si using a vacuum induction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: furnace under an argon atmosphere. The alloy homogeneity was checked by microprobe analysis and was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: found to be good. The metallographic examination revealed the presence of a few oxide inclusions in an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: otherwise apparently single phase ferritic matrix.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: All studies were carried out with rotating disk electrodes of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (diameter 0.357 cm) insulated with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a PTFE shrinkable tubing. Experiments were performed at 6000 rpm (in part at 600 rpm) in 1 M HCl at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 25°C under a nitrogen atmosphere. A Ag/AgCl reference electrode in saturated KCl was used.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A potentiostat (Amel 549 or 551) driven by a potential step motor unit (Wenking SMP 72) was used to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: determine polarization curves. The potential was increased in steps of 20 mV 400 s⁻ '. The current was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: monitored on a X-t recorder. Measured pseudo steady state values were digitized and evaluated on an HP

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 9845B computer.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Pretreatment of the electrodes included grinding with emery paper and polishing with alumina powder

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in water to 1/4 μm finish. They were rinsed and cathodically prepolarized in the working electrolyte at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: -700 mV(SHE) for 10 min.

layout_dets.text: beam at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The electrodes to be analysed after cathodic prepolarization were held at a constant potential in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: active

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: , the low passive at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or the high passive potential region at +950

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mV(SHE), respectively.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The charge passed was measured with a digital integrator (Amel 731). At the end of an experiment the

layout_dets.text: Anodic polarization curves of Cr, Mo, W and V in 1 M HCl are shown in Fig. 1.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: spontaneously passive or cannot be activated. Uniform transpassive dissolution of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mo and V sets in at potentials of approx. 550 mV(SHE), and of Cr at approx. 1250

layout_dets.text: mV(SHE). Tungsten exhibits a very low anodic current density up to potentials of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in HCl.

layout_dets.text: The mechanism for passive film breakdown leading to pitting is still not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The occurrence of pitting in binary iron-chromium alloys is known to depend on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the Cr/Fe ratio, i.e. on the activity of iron. Adding V decreases the iron activity in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloy and thus is expected to diminish susceptibility to pitting. Whether such an effect

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interface²5 or a change in repassivation kinetics on a film in dynamic equilibrium²

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cannot be decided at present.
